title: Outline-occluder shader — bombers visible as coloured outline when hidden behind hard blocks + cliffs
intent: When variable cell height ships (GDP-2026-05-28-010), bombers walking onto plateaus + cliff-bordered terrain will frequently be partially or fully hidden behind cliff geometry from the camera's POV. Same issue exists today on flat arenas with hard blocks — a bomber behind a hard wall is invisible from the camera, but the player needs to track them. The outline-occluder shader (already named in `visual-style.md §3` as the planned solution but never shipped) renders an outline of occluded bombers through the geometry — visible as a glow in the bomber's primary palette colour. Standard gameplay readability pattern (Diablo IV, Path of Exile, Overwatch ult outlines etc.). Solves a real readability gap before it becomes acute with height.
rationale: Source: `docs/game-design/visual-style.md §3` shader catalogue (named, status 'allowed' but never shipped) + forward-looking compatibility with GDP-2026-05-28-010 (variable height — cliffs occlude bombers). Marked `could` because flat arenas mostly avoid the issue today (camera framing keeps bombers in clear lines-of-sight); becomes more urgent post-heights. Small shader story, ~80 LOC.
acceptanceHints: examples/kaboom-crew/src/shaders/outline-occluder.ts: NEW shader implementation.

PURPOSE: render an outline silhouette of bomber meshes when they're OCCLUDED by world geometry (hard blocks, cliff faces, etc.). Silhouette appears as a glowing line in the bomber's primary palette colour, visible THROUGH the occluding geometry.
IMPLEMENTATION (Three.js):
Two-pass render approach using existing PostProcessing if available, OR a simpler dual-render:
Pass 1 — render scene normally (occluder + occluded both rendered).

Pass 2 — render bomber meshes again with depthTest=false + a coloured-outline shader (e.g. inverted hull or screen-space edge-detect via Three.js `OutlinePass`). Composite Pass 2 ONLY where Pass 1's depth value > the bomber's actual depth (i.e. where the bomber is occluded).
Result: visible bombers render normally; occluded bombers also render an outline.
ALTERNATIVE simpler shader-only path:

Per bomber: render a second MeshRenderer of the bomber tree with depthFunc=GREATER + a thin emissive outline material in the bomber's primary palette. Outline shader is fresnel-edge-based (existing pattern from S102 character-toon).
Works without a render pass extension — just a second material on the same mesh nodes. Recommended for simplicity in v1.
TAG SCOPE:
Only PlayerControlled + BotBrain entities get the outline-occluder treatment. Non-bomber entities (bombs, pickups, blocks, ramps, particles) don't need it — they don't move in tactical-relevant ways.
Local-player bomber: outline ALSO appears when the player's own bomber is behind geometry (helpful for navigation, especially with closer camera from S163). Could opt-out via URL.
Remote-player bombers in multiplayer: outline always on per the GameDesign 'opponent state visible at glance' policy.
COLOUR:
Outline colour = bomber's recipe.palette.head — matches the bomber identity established by the procedural character generator. A red bomber's outline is red.
Intensity: half-bright (~0.5 emissive multiplier) so outline doesn't overwhelm the visible scene.
Width: 2 px screen-space. Thin enough to NOT obscure surrounding gameplay, thick enough to be legible.
VISUAL DETAIL:

Outline emerges from the BOMBER SILHOUETTE — the outermost-pixel boundary of the bomber's projected shape. Inner details (limbs, head outline against torso) NOT outlined — only the overall silhouette.
Slight subtle pulse (0.5Hz, ±10% intensity) — telegraphs 'this is a special-rendered indicator, not just a clipping bug'.
TURN OFF:
`?outlines=off` URL flag disables the outline-occluder entirely. Useful for screenshot tests + low-performance hardware.
Per-entity opt-out for non-bomber outlines (in case future content adds nameplate / pet entities that don't need outlines).
PERFORMANCE:

Two-pass renders cost ~2× geometry render time for the BOMBER meshes only — ~50 vertices per bomber × 4 bombers = trivial. Pass 1 + Pass 2 cost combined is ~1ms / frame on a modern laptop. Within budget.
If using single-render dual-material approach: just adds one extra material per bomber. Negligible.
MULTIPLAYER: each client renders outlines for the bombers it sees. No network change.
INTERACTIONS:
With death ragdoll (S105+S128): outline disappears when bomber's alive=false (the alive flip removes the bomber entity's player/bot tag). Ragdoll body renders normally without outline.
With shield bubble: shield-bubble shader from S109 already wraps the bomber — outline-occluder + shield-bubble coexist; outline reads the bomber's primary, bubble reads palette.accent.
With sudden death walls (S160): the shrinking-wall blocks count as occluders. Bomber behind a closing wall shows outline.
With variable height + ramps (GDP-2026-05-28-010 / -011): cliff faces are occluders; outline shows bomber on the other side. THIS is the primary forward-looking value.
UNIT TESTS:
Outline material applied to bomber meshes at spawn time.
Outline colour = recipe.palette.head.
alive=false flip → outline material removed.
`?outlines=off` → outline material not applied.
Pulse animation: outline intensity oscillates between 0.45 and 0.55 over time.
VISUAL QA:
Bomber walks behind a hard block → outline visible through the block in the bomber's primary colour.
Bomber walks behind a cliff (post GDP-010) → outline visible.
Bomber walks into clear view → outline fades (depthFunc=GREATER means outline doesn't render when bomber is fully visible).
4 bombers each with different palette → 4 distinct outline colours.
Subtle pulse visible but not distracting.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Outlining bombs / pickups when occluded (not as gameplay-critical to track).
Outlining UI elements / waypoints.
Through-wall combat (the outline is INFORMATION only; bombers still fully blocked by walls for gameplay purposes).
Customisable outline colour (matches palette.head, not opt-in different colour).
Distance-fade for outlines (always visible regardless of distance — bomber position matters at any distance).
Outline-on-static-objects (e.g. outlined pickups always-visible). Bomber-specific.
